catalog_quote: 本稿で議論するカムチベット語諸方言では、強勢が音声学的な卓立を伴って現れることはないため、強勢が音体系上機能していると言うことができない。超分節音的音特徴にはおよそ明瞭な強勢の特徴が認められず、逆にチベット言語学上奇妙な現象が分節音に起きている。この現象を説明するために、「強さを伴わない架空の強勢パターン」（これを韻律特徴と呼ぶ）を設けて議論してみる。[...] • カムチベット語得榮徳欽方言群の諸方言は、基本的に「弱強型」の韻律特徴をもつ。•「弱強型」の韻律特徴は、第１音節の分節音に何らかの変化が生じる。• ただし、例外的に「強弱型」の韻律特徴をもつ方言を認める。•「強弱型」の韻律特徴は、第１音節に強勢が実際に置かれることで実現することが多い。韻律特徴は、その性格上、複音節語（音韻語）の初頭２音節（声調が機能する単位）に対してのみ適用される。[p.4] いずれの２音節語の場合も第２音節に強勢が音声学的に強さを伴って現れることはない。また、３音節以上からなる場合にもこの現象が現れることがあるが、３音節以降は軽声であるため無視できる。[p.9, quoting 鈴木 2012d:60 on mBalhag:] 複音節語について語単独での発音では、第１音節に聴覚印象として明瞭な強勢が置かれる例が存在する。強勢が置かれた場合、その直後すなわち第２音節以降の声調が低平調で実現される。また、第２音節以降に強勢が置かれる例は認められない。しかしながら、強勢の実現は現段階の資料において対立が認められず、かつ自由変異であり、現れても現れなくても許容されるため、一律表記しない。

new_statements.quote: 本稿で議論するカムチベット語諸方言では、強勢が音声学的な卓立を伴って現れることはないため、強勢が音体系上機能していると言うことができない。超分節音的音特徴にはおよそ明瞭な強勢の特徴が認められず、逆にチベット言語学上奇妙な現象が分節音に起きている。[…] • カムチベット語得榮徳欽方言群の諸方言は、基本的に「弱強型」の韻律特徴をもつ。•「弱強型」の韻律特徴は、第１音節の分節音に何らかの変化が生じる。• ただし、例外的に「強弱型」の韻律特徴をもつ方言を認める。•「強弱型」の韻律特徴は、第１音節に強勢が実際に置かれることで実現することが多い。[p.4:] いずれの２音節語の場合も第２音節に強勢が音声学的に強さを伴って現れることはない。また、３音節以上からなる場合にもこの現象が現れることがあるが、３音節以降は軽声であるため無視できる。
new_statements.translation: In the Khams Tibetan dialects discussed here, stress never appears accompanied by phonetic prominence, so one cannot say that stress functions in the sound system. Hardly any clear stress feature is found among the suprasegmental properties; instead, phenomena that are odd for Tibetan linguistics occur in the segments. [...] • The dialects of the Khams Tibetan sDerong-nJol (Derong-Deqin) group basically have a 'weak-strong' (iambic) prosodic feature. • Under the weak-strong prosodic feature some change arises in the segments of the first syllable. • Exceptionally, however, dialects with a 'strong-weak' (trochaic) prosodic feature are recognised. • The strong-weak prosodic feature is mostly realised by stress actually being placed on the first syllable. [p.4:] In none of these disyllabic words does stress appear on the second syllable with phonetic intensity. The phenomenon may also appear in words of three or more syllables, but the third syllable onward is 'light' (toneless) and can be ignored.
new_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki 鈴木博之. 2013. カムチベット語sDerong-nJol（得榮徳欽）方言群の諸方言における弱強型の韻律特徴と分節音に見えるその反映形. 地球研言語記述論集 5 (RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Series 5), 1–15.
new_statements.locator: §1–2, p.2 (bulleted summary p.2); §3.1, p.4; mBalhag subgroup §4.1 p.9; summary table §5 p.11
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (text of the PDF we hold, pages split on form feeds; printed folios match). p.2 opens exactly with 「本稿で議論するカムチベット語諸方言では、強勢が音声学的な卓立を伴って現れることはないため、強勢が音体系上機能していると言うことができない 2 。超分節音的音特徴にはおよそ明瞭な強勢の特徴が認められず、逆にチベット言語学上奇妙な現象が分節音に起きている。」 followed by section 2 with the four bullets exactly as quoted (弱強型 basic for the 得榮徳欽 group; change in syllable-1 segments; exceptional 強弱型 dialects; 強弱型 mostly realised as actual stress on syllable 1). Footnote 2 on the same page adds that in pitch-tone Tibetic varieties stress is expected to have no suprasegmental phonetic realisation and the term 'stress' is used only where a clear suprasegmental feature is present. p.4 first lines: 「いずれの２音節語の場合も第２音節に強勢が音声学…
new_statements.rule_in_words: sDerong-nJol Khams is a word-tone language (four pitch patterns realised over the first two syllables of the phonological word; syllables 3+ toneless/low). Suzuki states there is no phonetically prominent, phonologically functional word stress; he posits an abstract iambic (weak-strong) template over the first two syllables for most of the group (sDerong, West Yunling Mountain incl. Tsharethong/Sakar, sPomtserag subgroups), evidenced only by segmental weakening of syllable 1 (deaspiration, /a/-reduction). The mBalhag subgroup instead is trochaic: an audible but non-contrastive, optional stress on the first syllable of polysyllables in isolation, never on later syllables (Suzuki 2012 Minpaku 37(1): 60; Tournadre & Suzuki 2023: 242). gYagrwa subgroup: neither pattern needed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; syllables from the third onward are 'light' (軽声, toneless, low level) in all varieties.
new_statements.exceptions: Iambic weakening is speech-rate dependent (absent in slow, syllable-by-syllable elicitation) and partly lexicalised (e.g. Zulung has words that keep aspiration); mBalhag first-syllable stress requires syllable 1 to be a non-affix (prefixed verbs do not show it) and is in free variation; gYagrwa and mBalhag subgroups excluded from the iambic pattern.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the first two syllables of the phonological word (root + affixes) = the tone domain; statements based on citation/isolation forms and natural-rate speech; the 'prosodic feature' is explicitly called non-phonological by the author.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog sder1236 'Derong-nJol Tibetan' [tsk] = Suzuki's sDerong-nJol dialect group of Khams (dialects: Bodgrong bodg1236, Tseku tsek1238, Tsharethong tsha1248, gYagrwa gyag1236, mBalhag mbal1265, sPomtserag spom1236). The quoted statement (Suzuki 2013) covers the group as a whole and explicitly differentiates subgroups: iambic/no phonetic stress for sDerong, West Yunling Mountain (Tsharethong, Sakar, Zulung, Adong..) and sPomtserag subgroups; trochaic optional initial stress for the mBalhag subgroup (mbal1265; primary description Suzuki 2012 Minpaku 37(1) p.60, data from Bala, Shangri-La); gYagrwa (gyag1236) unspecified. Note Tournadre & Suzuki 2023 list Melung/mBalhag-area varieties partly under Semkyi Nyida rather than Derong-nJol, and Tshawarong under Dzayul; Glottolog follows Suzuki's later grouping. ISO tsk 'Tseku' is Glottolog's code assignment for this group.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki 鈴木博之. 2014. 怒江州のカムチベット語丙中洛［Bodgrong］方言の方言特徴 [Dialectal characteristics of the Bodgrong (Bingzhongluo) dialect of Khams Tibetan, Nujiang Prefecture]. ニダバ (Nidaba) 43: 40-49. 西日本言語学会.
tone_statements.quote: Bodgrong方言の音体系は以下のようである。【音節構造】最大でᶜCᵢGVCC。注：音節末子音が2つ存在する場合、最後の1つは/ʔ/である。【声調】語声調で、¯：高平、´：上昇、`：下降、^：上昇下降の4種。【母音】各要素に対応する長母音・鼻母音が存在する。 ... ここでは初頭子音と母音＋末子音の2種に分けて、蔵文とBodgrong方言との音対応について述べる。声調に関する議論は行わない。
tone_statements.translation: The sound system of the Bodgrong dialect is as follows. [Syllable structure] at most ᶜCᵢGVCC. Note: when there are two syllable-final consonants, the last one is /ʔ/. [Tone] Word tone, of 4 kinds: ¯ high level, ´ rising, ` falling, ^ rising-falling. [Vowels] Corresponding long and nasal vowels exist for each member. ... Here the sound correspondences between Written Tibetan and the Bodgrong dialect are described in two parts, initial consonants and vowel + final consonant. Tone is not discussed.
tone_statements.locator: p. 41, sec. 2 'Bodgrong方言の音体系概観', the 【声調】 line; continuation 'declares tone not discussed' at p. 42, sec. 3 intro
tone_statements.summary: Word tone with four types: high level, rising, falling, rising-falling, marked on every cited form; the Written-Tibetan correspondence sections set tone aside. Nothing on stress in the pages read.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki. 2013. Extraordinary sound development of *s and *z in mBalhag Tibetan (Shangri-La, Yunnan). Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 36(1): 101-110.
tone_statements.quote: This section presents examples and a phonetic description of WrT s and z sound correspondences in the mBalhag dialect.7 ... 7 The phonetic description includes the IPA symbols and necessary non-IPA symbols defined in Zhu (2010). The tone is described as a word-tone system, which is transcribed with the following signs: ¯ : high level ´ : rising ^ : rising-falling/low level ` : falling
tone_statements.locator: p. 102, sec. 2 'Phonetic description', footnote 7; tone-marked forms throughout sec. 2-3, pp. 103-106
tone_statements.summary: Footnote only: a word-tone system written with four signs per word (high level, rising, rising-falling/low level, falling); about 100 forms carry one word-tone mark each; no further tone analysis.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki 鈴木博之. 2010. カムチベット語燕門／斯嘎［Yanmen / Sakar］方言の方言特徴 [Dialectal characteristics of the Yanmen/Sakar dialect of Khams Tibetan]. ニダバ (Nidaba) 39: 78-87. 西日本言語学会.
tone_statements.quote: Sakar方言の音体系は以下のようである。【音節構造】最大でᶜCᵢGVCC、初頭子音が鼻音のときCCGVCCもある。 ... 【声調】語声調で、ˉ：高平、´：上昇、`：下降、ˆ：上昇下降の4種。【母音】各要素に対応する長母音・鼻母音が存在する。 ... ここでは初頭子音と母音＋末子音の2種に分けて、蔵文とSakar方言との音対応について述べる。声調に関する議論は行わない。
tone_statements.translation: The sound system of the Sakar dialect is as follows. [Syllable structure] maximally ᶜCᵢGVCC; when the initial consonant is a nasal, CCGVCC also occurs. ... [Tone] Word tone, four kinds: ˉ high level, ´ rising, ` falling, ˆ rising-falling. [Vowels] For each element there are corresponding long and nasal vowels. ... Here, dividing into initial consonants and vowel+final consonant, I describe the sound correspondences between Written Tibetan and the Sakar dialect. Tone is not discussed.
tone_statements.locator: p.79, §2 'Sakar方言の音体系概観', 【声調】 line; 'tone is not discussed' sentence = §3 intro, end of p.79 to top of p.80
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Word tone with four tones: high level, rising, falling and rising-falling, written as one mark before each word; given in the sound-system overview; the paper does not discuss tone further.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki 鈴木博之. 2008. 迪慶州瀾滄江流域カムチベット語（徳欽／雲嶺／燕門／巴迪方言）の方言特徴 [Dialectal characteristics of Khams Tibetan along the Lancang river in Diqing Prefecture: Deqin, Yunling, Yanmen and Badi dialects]. ニダバ (Nidaba) 37: 115-124. 西日本言語学会.
tone_statements.quote: 2 音体系の素描 各種方言ともそれぞれの音素体系は似通っているが、若干異なりもある。ここでは、Yungling方言の例を掲げる。【音節構造】最大でCCiGVC、初頭子音が鼻音のときCCVCもある。【声調】語声調で、¯：高平、´：上昇、`：下降、^：上昇下降の4種。【母音】各要素に対応する長母音・鼻母音が存在する。
tone_statements.translation: 2 Sketch of the sound system. The phoneme systems of the various dialects resemble one another, though there are some slight differences. Here I give the Yungling dialect as the example. [Syllable structure] At most CCiGVC; CCVC also occurs when the initial consonant is a nasal. [Tone] Word tone, of 4 kinds: ¯ high level, ´ rising, ` falling, ^ rising-falling. [Vowels] Long vowels and nasal vowels corresponding to each element exist.
tone_statements.locator: p. 116, sec. 2 音体系の素描, 【声調】 line
tone_statements.summary: Word tone with four patterns (high level, rising, falling, rising-falling), stated for Yungling as representative of the nJol-group dialects; every cited form carries one of the four marks.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki 鈴木博之. 2007. 川西民族走廊・チベット語方言研究 [Study of the Tibetan dialects of the Ethnic Corridor of West Sichuan]. PhD dissertation (博士(文学), 甲第12734号), Kyoto University. xxviii+420 pp. + supplement volume.
tone_statements.quote: 超分節音 声調で４種が認められる ¯：高平 ´：上昇 `：下降 ˆ：低/上昇下降 ... 筆者の分析によって、チベット語方言の場合、声調は音節声調としてではなく語声調として扱うことができるという結果を得ており、本論文を通して語声調としてデータを提示する。この場合、声調は型（調類）が問題となり、調値は問題としない。 ... また、当然語を構成する音節数が多ければ、その中に声調を担わない音節（第３音節以降および一部の第２音節）も現れるが、それには特別表記を与えない。
tone_statements.translation: Suprasegmentals: four tone types are recognised: ¯ high level, ´ rising, ` falling, ˆ low / rising-falling ... By the author's analysis, in Tibetan dialects tone can be treated not as syllable tone but as word tone, and throughout this thesis the data are presented as word tone. In that case it is the type (tone category) that matters, not the pitch value. ... Also, if a word consists of many syllables, syllables that bear no tone (the third syllable onward and some second syllables) naturally appear, but no special marking is given to them.
tone_statements.locator: §4.22.1 音素一覧 (sDerong 方言), p.178; joined with §3.3.2 超分節音素の表記法, p.55; cf. §4.25.1 p.192 Yungling and §4.26.1 p.197 Budy, same header; §5.2.3 pp.215-216
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: SDerong: four word-tone types, high level, rising, falling, low/rising-falling; Yunling and Badi also four; the tone unit is the word and third and later syllables carry no tone; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki (2012). Khams-Tibettogo Yunling-Chalitong [Tsharethong] hoogen no onsei bunseki. Asian and African Languages and Linguistics (AALL) 7. pp. 155-194.
tone_statements.quote: Tsharethong 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高平調、上昇調、下降調、上昇下降調の４種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。ただし３音節以上の語の場合、第１、第２音節までで弁別的な声調の型を形成し、第３音節以降は [22] 程度の高さで現れる。 [...] Tsharethong 方言の声調体系は、語声調で語頭の音節初頭部が高いか低いかの異なりと音節末尾で下降するかしないかの２通りで構成され、計４種の弁別が行われる。
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3 超分節音, printed p. 158; sec. 6.3 声調, printed pp. 169-170; tone marks listed in sec. 2.1, p. 157
tone_statements.check: quotation from the author's open copy, read 2026-09-25; not yet verified by a second reading
tone_statements.summary: Translation of the deciding passage: 'The distinctive suprasegmental in Tsharethong is a tonal contrast by pitch height, of four kinds: high level, rising, falling, rising-falling. sources.quote: Tsharethong 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高平調、上昇調、下降調、上昇下降調の４種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。ただし３音節以上の語の場合、第１、第２音節までで弁別的な声調の型を形成し、第３音節以降は [22] 程度の高さで現れる。 [...] Tsharethong 方言の声調体系は、語声調で語頭の音節初頭部が高いか低いかの異なりと音節末尾で下降するかしないかの２通りで構成され、計４種の弁別が行われる。
sources.locator: sec. 3 超分節音, printed p. 158; sec. 6.3 声調, printed pp. 169-170; tone marks listed in sec. 2.1, p. 157
sources.note: Translation of the deciding passage: 'The distinctive suprasegmental in Tsharethong is a tonal contrast by pitch height, of four kinds: high level, rising, falling, rising-falling. They apply to the word as a unit. In words of three or more syllables the distinctive tone pattern is formed on the first and second syllables, and the third syllable onward appears at about [22].' Sec. 6.3: 'The tone system is a word-tone system built from two binary choices, whether the onset of the word-initial syllable is high or low and whether there is a fall at the syllable end, giving four contrasts.' tone.translation: The sound system of the Bodgrong dialect is as follows. [Syllable structure] at most ᶜCᵢGVCC. Note: when there are two syllable-final consonants, the last one is /ʔ/. [Tone] Word tone, of 4 kinds: ¯ high level, ´ rising, ` falling, ^ rising-falling. [Vowels] Corresponding long and nasal vowels exist for each member. ... Here the sound correspondences between Written Tibetan and the Bodgrong dialect are described in two parts, initial consonants and vowel + final consonant. Tone is not discussed.

sources.note: Examples are marked for word tone ('語単位にかかる語声調') with five word-initial symbols ¯ high level, ´ rising, ` falling, _ low level, ˆ rising-falling; among features relevant to subgrouping, the high/low tone onset of the sample words agrees across the Diqing dialects (except 'snake'), 'chicken'/'Tibetan' begin voiceless with low pitch; fn.5: as in mBathang and Derge, the tone of etymologically voiced stops/affricates does not split by rule, high and low tones both occur. Tone typology is named as a criterion for Khams membership, not for fine subgrouping.

tone.translation: Below, examples are given from the Thoteng dialect, which belongs to the Sems-kyi-nyila dialect group. [Syllable structure] At most ᶜCᵢGVC; CCVC also occurs when the initial consonant is a nasal. [Tone] Word tone, of 4 kinds: ˉ high level, ´ rising, ` falling, ^ rising-falling.
